analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md. Per file_changes, the changes are at base lines 1841/1864 and head 1841/1864-1871: the sampling-defaults table row and a paragraph stating that catalog Qwen 3.5/3.6 builds (Qwen3.5-9B, qwen3.5-35b-a3b, qwen3.6-35b-a3b-vl-mtp-mxfp8) take model-card defaults (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5) when they ship no generation_config.json. The supplied units are the BASE text at lines 2429-2954, which lie outside the changed hunks and contain only unchanged surrounding documentation. I examined them against the threat model. They cover MiMo ingress and decode memory accounting, Flint constraints, coordinator-serving channels, the refusal-log invariant (no request text), add-on hold refusals, the Autopilot hold, and the Bonsai MTP notes.

The patch is documentation only. It alters no code, authorization, encryption, attestation or cache-storage control. The cited sampling-default change (EngineV2SamplingDefaults.qwen35CardDefaults) is described as a quality fix for repetition until max_tokens (#1530). That could slightly shorten runaway GPU use (T-010, T-029 are DoS-adjacent), but the code is not supplied, so I draw no security conclusion. The patch adds no new data exposure and does not touch the T-041 prefix-cache posture (HMAC names, 30-minute TTL, account-scoped salt). The one cross-file question for later passes: whether the code behind this documentation (EngineV2SamplingDefaults, EngineV2Bridge+Translation.swift samplingParams) applies the new presence_penalty default only to the bound model_types and does not let unrelated models or identities pick up the card defaults. This source-only pass cannot verify that. No threat-model update is needed because the change introduces no new boundary or asset.
